system.title: LG M50 fast-charge protocol, PyBaMM DFN with plating and lumped thermal

solver.name: PyBaMM
solver.validity: 0.2-1.5C steps, 23-27 degC within range, 5-40 degC extrapolation; charge above 0.3C unvalidated by records; computational only

objective.statement: Charge the LG M50 from 10 to 80 % faster than the failing 1.5C four-step baseline while the anode potential stays at or above +10 mV vs Li/Li+ and the cell at or below 45 degC. The ambient is 25 degC: every simulated protocol runs at ambient = 25 degC.

constraints.label: Plating margin: anode potential at or above +25 mV

amendments.author: engineer
amendments.reason: Raise the plating margin to +25 mV. The model's voltage gap to the records is 70–160 mV, so +10 mV is not a safe margin.

fails: Plating margin: anode potential at or above +25 mV: min_anode_potential is 7.304 ± 0.5 mV, outside >= 25 mV
Cell at or below 45 degC: max_temperature is 51.191 ± 0.1 degC, outside <= 45 degC

current_result.sentence: In simulation, Simulate a four-step fast charge from 10 to 80 % SOC: ambient 25 degC, c_rate_1 1.5 1/h, c_rate_2 1.25 1/h, c_rate_3 1.2 1/h, c_rate_4 0.8 1/h: Time from 10 to 80 % SOC 37.275 min against 28.203 min for the baseline; min_anode_potential 26.181 mV (limit >= 25); max_temperature 44.826 degC (limit <= 45); better than the baseline, which fails Plating margin: anode potential at or above +25 mV and Cell at or below 45 degC; meeting the limits costs 9.072 min.

requests.rationale: Re-run the baseline configuration of chen2020-lgm50/failing-baseline-1p5c on the solver, so computational candidates are compared with a computational baseline.

Hypothesis: Temperature, accumulated mainly from sustained high early/mid current, is the binding constraint, while anode potential only approaches its limit late in charge. Keeping 1.5C only in the first low-SOC step and stepping down thereafter should raise the late-charge anode minimum well above 10 mV, but the longer charge may still leave peak temperature near or above 45 degC.

Baseline res_6c647caf0bc81ae5fb537157 at 1.5C throughout gave 28.203 min but min_anode_potential 7.304 mV (fails >=10 mV) and max_temperature 51.191 degC (fails <=45 degC). Its series show anode potential falling toward the minimum only at high SOC and temperature rising monotonically, so a descending step protocol tests whether late-current reduction fixes plating while revealing whether accumulated heat still binds. Ambient is fixed at 25 degC per objective.

Hypothesis: Late-charge anode potential, not peak temperature, now limits charge time: in res_3d7d57ac34d44fe437184940 temperature peaked at 42.426 degC at the end of step 3 and fell during the 0.8C step 4, while anode potential fell monotonically in step 4 to its 24.114 mV minimum at 80% SOC. Raising only step 4 should therefore cut time with little change in peak temperature, but will consume much of the 14.114 mV anode slack.

Baseline res_6c647caf0bc81ae5fb537157 (1.5C throughout) failed both constraints: 7.304 mV and 51.191 degC in 28.203 min. The stepped candidate res_3d7d57ac34d44fe437184940 (1.5/1.2/1.0/0.8C) passed both at 24.114 mV and 42.426 degC but took 39.375 min; my temperature prediction for it was high (47 degC predicted vs 42.426 measured, outside interval), so I revise temperature expectations downward. Its series show peak temperature before step 4 and the anode minimum at the end of step 4, so isolating a step-4 increase to 1.1C is the most decision-relevant test: nominal four-step time falls to 35.80 min while steps 1-3, which set the temperature peak, are unchanged. Ambient fixed at 25 degC per objective; all rates within 0.2-1.5C bounds and within the stated validity range.

Hypothesis: Late-charge anode potential in step 4, not mid-charge anode, limits the protocol, while peak temperature is set by cumulative heating approximated by the sum of step C-rates. Raising steps 2 and 3 equally to 1.25C (keeping step 4 at the already-binding 1.1C and step 1 at 1.5C) cuts time heat-efficiently: mid-charge anode minima (~41-48 mV in res_30c23ad068919d9f89d45ecd) have large slack, but the higher cumulative heat will push peak temperature close to 45 degC and may slightly lower the step-4 anode minimum.

Incumbent res_30c23ad068919d9f89d45ecd (1.5/1.2/1.0/1.1C) passed at 35.814 min, 10.775 mV (0.775 mV slack) and 43.767 degC (1.233 degC slack). Its series show the anode minimum at the end of step-4 CC just before CV entry, whereas step 2/3 end anode values were ~48/~41 mV, so raising only steps 2-3 avoids directly increasing the binding step-4 current. Temperature rose monotonically to its end-of-charge peak; scaling its 18.767 degC rise by the C-rate-sum ratio 5.1/4.8 gives ~44.9 degC, so temperature is the expected near-binding risk of this move. Equal 1.25C in steps 2-3 minimises sum(1/C) for a given sum(C) heat proxy. Ambient fixed at 25 degC per objective; all rates within 0.2-1.5C bounds and within the stated validity range.

Hypothesis: Peak temperature, set by cumulative heating from steps 2-3, is now the binding constraint, while the step-4 anode minimum has recovered slack. In res_7485b76eaac648a546edfcbf (1.5/1.25/1.25/1.1C) temperature failed at 45.41 degC but min_anode_potential improved to 13.034 mV versus 10.775 mV in the incumbent res_30c23ad068919d9f89d45ecd (1.5/1.2/1.0/1.1C, 43.767 degC). Raising only step 3 by 0.15C (60% of the failing run's step-3 increase, step 2 unchanged) should retain much of the time saving while pulling peak temperature ~0.7 degC below the 45 degC limit.

Comparison first: the last result res_7485b76eaac648a546edfcbf matched my prediction on all three quantities (33.346 min vs 33.4 predicted, 45.41 degC within [43.4,45.8], 13.034 mV within [7,16]) but violated max_temperature <=45 degC by 0.41 degC, so it is not a candidate. The incumbent res_30c23ad068919d9f89d45ecd passes at 35.814 min, 10.775 mV, 43.767 degC. The incumbent-to-failing difference (+0.05C step 2, +0.25C step 3) gave -2.468 min, +1.643 degC, +2.259 mV. Taking the step-3 portion alone at 0.15/0.25 = 60% of that move (1.5/1.2/1.15/1.1C) linearly predicts 34.4 min (nominal four-step time 10.5*(1/1.5+1/1.2+1/1.15+1/1.1)=34.43 min, matching how earlier nominal times matched measured), 44.7 degC, 12.1 mV. This isolates the temperature-time tradeoff at fixed step 4. Ambient fixed at 25 degC per objective; all rates on the 0.05C grid within 0.2-1.5C bounds and 23-27 degC validity range.

Hypothesis: Under objective v2 the step-4 anode potential is the binding constraint, not temperature: the anode minimum occurs at the end of step 4. Reducing step 4 from 0.8C to 0.75C should raise that minimum above 25 mV, while raising steps 2-3 (where anode values remain ~35-48 mV) recovers charge time; the main risk is that cumulative mid-charge heating pushes peak temperature, which occurs late, over 45 degC.

Re-check under v2 (min_anode_potential >=25 mV, max_temperature <=45 degC): no earlier result passes. Baseline res_6c647caf0bc81ae5fb537157: 7.304 mV, 51.191 degC, 28.203 min. res_3d7d57ac34d44fe437184940 (1.5/1.2/1.0/0.8C) is closest: 24.114 mV (fails by only 0.886 mV), 42.426 degC, 39.375 min. res_30c23ad068919d9f89d45ecd (same steps 1-3, step 4 raised to 1.1C): 10.775 mV, 43.767 degC, 35.814 min — so +0.3C on step 4 alone costs 13.339 mV (~44 mV per C), identifying step 4 as binding. Its series and res_3d7d57ac34d44fe437184940 confirm the anode minimum at the end of step 4, while step 2/3 anode values stay ~35-48 mV. Last result res_08e02c1eaff26cbb13617b06 matched my previous prediction (34.431 min, 44.691 degC, 11.982 mV) but fails v2 on anode. Raising steps 2-3 earlier (res_30c23ad068919d9f89d45ecd -> res_7485b76eaac648a546edfcbf / res_08e02c1eaff26cbb13617b06) did not lower the step-4 anode minimum (it rose to 13.034/11.982 mV) but raised temperature ~5.5 degC per unit summed mid C-rate. Prediction: nominal time 10.5*(1/1.5+1/1.35+1/1.25+1/0.75)=37.18 min; anode 24.114 + ~2.2 mV from -0.05C step 4 + ~1.5 mV warmer-history effect = ~27.8 mV; temperature 42.426 + ~2.2 degC from +0.40 summed mid rate - ~0.2 degC from lower step 4 = ~44.4 degC. Ambient fixed at 25 degC per objective; all rates within 0.2-1.5C bounds and within stated validity range.

Hypothesis: Under objective v2, peak temperature from cumulative mid-charge heating is now the binding constraint, not the step-4 anode minimum. The last run res_f27b0f455db60b53a3e3c13c (1.5/1.35/1.25/0.75C) gave min_anode_potential 29.539 mV (4.539 mV slack over >=25 mV) but max_temperature 45.834 degC, failing <=45 degC and falling outside my predicted hi of 45.6 degC — so I revise the mid-rate heating coefficient upward. Reducing steps 2-3 summed rate by 0.20C at unchanged 0.75C step 4 should cut peak temperature by ~1.5-1.7 degC while retaining most anode slack, at a cost of ~1.3 min.

Comparison first: res_f27b0f455db60b53a3e3c13c matched my time prediction (37.178 vs 37.2 min) and anode prediction (29.539 within [24,32] mV) but temperature 45.834 degC was outside [42.8,45.6] degC, so my temperature model under-predicts mid-rate heating; I now weight the observed res_3d7d57ac34d44fe437184940 -> res_f27b0f455db60b53a3e3c13c change more heavily: +0.40C summed steps 2-3 (and -0.05C step 4) raised peak temperature 42.426 -> 45.834 degC, i.e. ~8.5 degC per summed C. Re-check under v2 (>=25 mV, <=45 degC): still no earlier result passes both; the closest remains res_3d7d57ac34d44fe437184940 at 24.114 mV / 42.426 degC / 39.375 min. This proposal (1.5/1.25/1.15/0.75C) has nominal time 10.5*(1/1.5+1/1.25+1/1.15+1/0.75)=38.53 min; temperature predicted as 45.834 - 0.20*8.5 = ~44.1-44.3 degC; anode held at 0.75C step 4 should stay near 28 mV, allowing for a small loss of the warmer-history benefit seen when mid rates rose. Ambient fixed at 25 degC per objective; all rates within 0.2-1.5C bounds and within the stated validity range. This is the most decision-relevant next test because it isolates the temperature retreat needed for a first v2-feasible candidate while preserving the anode-passing step-4 rate.

Hypothesis: Under objective v2 the step-4 anode potential is the binding constraint for further time reduction, with temperature second: the anode minimum occurs at the end of step 4, and raising step 4 from 0.8C to 1.1C at fixed steps 1-3 (res_3d7d57ac34d44fe437184940 -> res_30c23ad068919d9f89d45ecd) cost 13.339 mV (~44 mV per C) but only 1.341 degC. The incumbent res_4e9366df1358ee1c750c3f1b has 3.351 mV anode slack, enough for a +0.05C step-4 increase (~2.2 mV cost), while its 0.684 degC temperature slack should absorb the ~0.2 degC step-4 heating. Raising steps 2-3 instead is worse: +0.20C summed mid rate (res_4e9366df1358ee1c750c3f1b -> res_f27b0f455db60b53a3e3c13c direction) cost ~1.5 degC for less time saved.

Comparison first: the last result res_4e9366df1358ee1c750c3f1b (1.5/1.25/1.15/0.75C) matched my prediction on all three quantities (38.53 min vs 38.5, 44.316 degC vs 44.3, 28.351 mV vs 28.0, all inside intervals) and is the first result to pass both v2 constraints (>=25 mV, <=45 degC), at 38.53 min. Re-check under v2: every earlier result fails at least one constraint; baseline is 7.304 mV / 51.191 degC. This proposal changes only step 4, 0.75C -> 0.8C, isolating the binding quantity. Nominal time 10.5*(1/1.5+1/1.25+1/1.15+1/0.8) = 37.66 min, matching the nominal-equals-measured pattern of the non-CV runs. Anode predicted as 28.351 - 0.05*44.5 = ~26.1 mV; temperature as 44.316 + ~0.2 = ~44.5 degC. Ambient fixed at 25 degC per objective; all rates within 0.2-1.5C bounds and within the stated validity range.

Hypothesis: Under objective v2 the step-4 anode potential binds against any further step-4 increase, while a small step-3 increase is limited mainly by cumulative heating: raising step 4 by 0.05C in the last run cost 2.627 mV (28.351 to 25.724 mV, ~52 mV per C), leaving only 0.724 mV anode slack, whereas temperature has 0.684 degC slack and earlier summed mid-rate increases cost ~8.5 degC per summed C, so +0.05C on step 3 alone should cost only ~0.4 degC and save ~0.38 min without directly raising the binding step-4 current.

Comparison first: the last result res_907ab80d5b4a52798de2393a (1.5/1.25/1.15/0.8C) matched my prediction on all three quantities (37.655 min vs 37.7, 44.316 degC vs 44.5, 25.724 mV vs 26.1, all inside intervals) and passes both v2 constraints (>=25 mV, <=45 degC), making it the incumbent at 37.655 min. Re-check under v2: it and res_4e9366df1358ee1c750c3f1b (38.53 min, 28.351 mV, 44.316 degC) are the only feasible results; all earlier results fail at least one v2 constraint. With 1 experiment remaining, the most decision-relevant test is the smallest time-saving move that does not touch the binding step-4 rate: step 3 from 1.15C to 1.20C gives the largest time saving per added C among the non-maxed mid steps (10.5/1.15^2 > 10.5/1.25^2 min per C). Nominal time 10.5*(1/1.5+1/1.25+1/1.20+1/0.8)=37.28 min; temperature predicted as 44.316 + 0.05*~8.5 = ~44.7 degC using the heating coefficient observed from res_3d7d57ac34d44fe437184940 to res_f27b0f455db60b53a3e3c13c; anode predicted near 25.9 mV since earlier mid-rate increases (res_30c23ad068919d9f89d45ecd to res_7485b76eaac648a546edfcbf / res_08e02c1eaff26cbb13617b06) did not lower the step-4 anode minimum. Ambient fixed at 25 degC per objective; all rates within 0.2-1.5C bounds and within the stated validity range.

conclusion.text:
Conclusion under objective version 2 (min_anode_potential >= 25 mV, max_temperature <= 45 degC, minimise charge_time_80; amendment seq 132 raised the anode limit from 10 to 25 mV):

Last result comparison first: res_16f97cc2073434bfe2d24230 (rq_77f33c2c47352e45d9a2, 1.5/1.25/1.20/0.8C, ambient 25 degC) matched the sealed prediction on all three quantities — charge_time_80 37.275 min vs 37.28 predicted [37.0, 37.6], max_temperature 44.826 degC vs 44.7 [44.0, 45.2], min_anode_potential 26.181 mV vs 25.9 [24.3, 27.5] — and passes both v2 constraints (cmp_3ca546948a2d45263541d220), with 1.181 mV anode slack and 0.174 degC temperature slack. It is the system incumbent at 37.275 min.

Re-check of all earlier results against v2: only three results pass both constraints — res_4e9366df1358ee1c750c3f1b (38.53 min, 28.351 mV, 44.316 degC), res_907ab80d5b4a52798de2393a (37.655 min, 25.724 mV, 44.316 degC) and res_16f97cc2073434bfe2d24230 (37.275 min, 26.181 mV, 44.826 degC), so the last is the fastest feasible candidate found. All others fail at least one v2 constraint, including the 1.5C baseline (28.203 min, 7.304 mV, 51.191 degC in the baseline computational comparison), res_f27b0f455db60b53a3e3c13c (29.539 mV but 45.834 degC, and its temperature fell outside the predicted interval, forcing the heating model upward), and the pre-v2 fast runs at step-4 1.1C (e.g. res_7485b76eaac648a546edfcbf, 13.034 mV, 45.41 degC).

Mechanism found: the step-4 anode minimum binds against step-4 rate (~44-52 mV lost per C of step-4 increase, from res_3d7d57ac34d44fe437184940 -> res_30c23ad068919d9f89d45ecd and res_4e9366df1358ee1c750c3f1b -> res_907ab80d5b4a52798de2393a), while cumulative mid-charge heating (~8.5 degC per summed C of steps 2-3) makes max_temperature jointly binding. Therefore no tested protocol is both v2-feasible and faster than the failing 28.203 min baseline: the fastest v2-feasible protocol, 1.5/1.25/1.20/0.8C at 25 degC, takes 37.275 min. Budget is spent (8/8 experiments used, 0 remaining), so the campaign ends with that candidate.
unresolved_reasons: No candidate met the constraints while beating the 28.203 min failing-baseline time; the fastest v2-feasible result is 37.275 min (res_16f97cc2073434bfe2d24230), so 'faster than baseline' and the v2 constraints appear jointly unattainable within the tested 0.2-1.5C step bounds at 25 degC.

All evidence is computational (PyBaMM DFN, OKane2022): the system validity notes state charge above 0.3C is unvalidated by records, the protocol is above the manufacturer's 0.7C charge rating, and no physical_confirmation was run, so the 37.275 min candidate (rq_77f33c2c47352e45d9a2) is not physically confirmed.

Temperature and anode margins of the incumbent are thin (0.174 degC and 1.181 mV, versus stated tolerances of 0.1 degC and 0.5 mV), and plated_lithium values are labelled indicative/unvalidated, so robustness to cell-to-cell variation and model error is unresolved.

The thermal model was never calibrated in this campaign (no calibrate_thermal result; solver heat-transfer coefficient remains the stated 6.0 W/m^2/K), leaving the near-binding temperature prediction dependent on the uncalibrated lumped model.
